method: Source-inspected positive cases and issue-specific negative controls, frozen before inspecting OCR findings. Not an exhaustive inventory. Repo comments and classroom labels make these intentionally vulnerable examples easier than production code.
execution: Static scan through Argus. No target installation, build, tests, application execution or exploit execution. No aggregate token budget. Existing 1800-second process deadline remains.

positives.reason: get_user interpolates request-derived username into SQL in the default vuln=1 branch.
Authenticated user can choose a different target username in update_password.
get_by_title retrieves another owner's book and secret without matching the authenticated owner.
Registration accepts the request's admin flag; schema permits additional properties.
Public debug handler returns all stored passwords, emails and admin flags.
Login distinguishes nonexistent users and incorrect passwords; secure branch uses one generic message.
Unbounded request email reaches ambiguous nested repetition; explicitly documented RegexDOS lesson.
Static public weak secret is used for HS256 token signing and verification.
Password stored directly and compared directly during login. Additional source-confirmed case beyond README labels.
Three request body fields reach eval before numeric validation; count as one root issue.
Raw threshold interpolated into MongoDB $where JavaScript; integer-sanitizing fix is commented out.
User ID comes from URL parameters rather than session; route only checks logged-in state.
User-controlled URL and symbol reach needle.get without destination restrictions.
Benefits operations require login but not isAdmin; commented secure routing is inactive.
Password inserted directly; bcrypt implementation is inside a comment.
Authenticated userId assigned without regenerating session ID.
CSRF middleware is commented out while cookie-authenticated mutation routes remain. Exploitability depends on browser/SameSite/deployment context; lower severity than direct injection.
Unrestricted req.query.url passed to res.redirect.
Hardcoded shared cookieSecret consumed by express-session.
Request accountName concatenated into WHERE clause then executed.
login_count parsed/bound but userid concatenated into PreparedStatement SQL.
User last_name concatenated; union checker grades attack and does not prevent execution.
Unrestricted request column concatenated before prepareStatement; prepared wrapper does not parameterize identifiers.
Request XML parsed with external entities/DTD enabled when secure=false.
Request Base64 token reaches ObjectInputStream.readObject without pre-deserialization filtering; type check occurs afterwards.
Lesson returns a profile for a different URL userId instead of enforcing ownership.
Lesson accepts another user's ID and submitted role/color without ownership authorization; changes stay in lesson session.
Single-pass keyword stripping and space checks feed an injectable query; not a parameterized query.

scoring_rules: Expected-case recall = matched positive cases / 28; each expected case counted once, regardless of duplicate findings.
A finding must identify the relevant unsafe behavior and code/function, not merely the file or a keyword.
Findings outside the expected list are reviewed separately; they are not automatically false positives.
Confirmed issue-specific negative-control claims are false positives; unrelated valid issues in the same file are not.
Report valid unique issues, duplicates, false positives, uncertain/deployment-dependent findings and out-of-scope nonsecurity findings separately.
If scan coverage is partial, report overall expected-case recall and coverage-qualified recall separately; never call incomplete coverage complete.
This is one run per selected source scope and one model. It does not establish run-to-run stability, production effectiveness or dynamic exploitability.
